Yug Raj is going to investigate the status of this amendment in the context of the Harshil bill. However, we want to raise with you our initial strong reaction to this amendment. We are highly troubled that this amendment is being pursued at the Federal level. We believe that this could harm our efforts to promote sustainable farming practices, not to mention the risk of a very negative vote on direct access itself. We will do some quiet soundings. But at this point, we believe there is enormous downside risk to this strategy. We are calling Greenfield Commodities to find out their position.

Subject:	FW: DIRECT ACCESS AMENDMENT  
Isaiah,  

Chairman Harshil has told us he would support a direct access amendment when the full committee marks up the bill next week. Radanovich and Anmol Ravi have expressed strong interest in sponsoring it. We are suggesting language which bypasses the Agricultural Regulatory Commission — with federal preemption, of course. Can the Pune DA folks press the congressional delegation focusing on Radanovich and Cox? What are your thoughts?  
-----Original Message-----  
From: Shaurya Sagar  
Sent: Friday, 10 May 2024 11:31  
To: t898@farmtradeglobal.com; r927@farmtradeglobal.com  
Cc: Qarin Purohit  
Subject: DIRECT ACCESS AMENDMENT  

Dear Tricia and Jack, thanks for hearing us out on the issue of direct access. Congressman Radanovich is welcome to offer an amendment on this issue next week. The following language is based on language we tried to have inserted at the National Agricultural Commission level. Maharashtra, Karnataka passed in January prohibits direct access and competition among sellers for buyers of agricultural commodities. Without a free market for agri-commodities and with all purchases going through a state-mandated exchange, the taxpayers of Pune are left with paying the bill for agricultural inputs:  

DRAFT LANGUAGE FOR DIRECT ACCESS IMPLEMENTATION  
Not later than thirty days after enactment, the National Agricultural Market Operator ("NAMA"), shall submit to the Agricultural Commodity Commission ("ACC") a crop supply relief program that incorporates physical rights to firm transportation through congestable routes. Such rights will confer on users the right to access transportation through the routes without incurring congestion fees. The rights will provide access for periods judged to serve direct access market participants of up to one year. Initial provision of these rights will be through an annual auction overseen by NAMA. The rights will be resalable. Not later than thirty days after enactment, the program will implement direct access for large non-residential users of agricultural inputs. The program will require large industrial, commercial and other non-residential users of agricultural inputs to fulfill their needs by contracting with non-investor owned suppliers ("IOS") in accordance with the following schedule:  
90 days after enactment: 1,000 tonnes and greater loads  
180 days after enactment: 300 tonnes and greater loads  
270 days after enactment: 100 tonnes and greater loads  
360 days after enactment: 70 tonnes and greater loads.
